claims.statement: Tranquilli, arXiv 2608.02675 v1 (the method source; NOT 2609.04686, which is Garcia): Prop. 3 and Lemmas 5-6 (a simple cubic bipartite graph without 4-cycles is the Levi graph of a linear v_3-configuration; Levi 8- and 16-cycles are Berge 4- and 8-cycles); Prop. 10 (the triangle-rooted, least-unfinished-point, lexicographic growth search is complete for connected configurations with a Berge triangle); Lemma 8 (Moore bound for girth 10); Lemma 9 (triangle roots, two orbits); Table 2 (cap-29 counters per orbit); Table 4 (leaf counts). Certified result of that paper: no counterexample up to 58 vertices.

Premise of route 1 only, orders 62-68: n(3,10) = 70, i.e. a cubic graph of girth at least 10 has at least 70 vertices (O'Keefe-Wong, JCTB 29 (1980) 91-105, computer assisted; completeness Wong 1983, McKay et al. 2000), read by the producer ONLY through the Exoo-Jajcay Dynamic Cage Survey (EJC DS16 v3, p. 7 Table 1, p. 10 Sec. 2.1.6). The original was not read by anyone. Together with the Moore bounds (girth 10: at least 62 vertices; girth 12: at least 126) it makes the triangle-rooted search sufficient for bipartite graphs of order at most 68. Route 2 (arbitrary root) does not use this premise.

Prior and parallel claims, as read: (a) A. V. Ripatti, BAIKAL/MOTOR 2017 one-page abstract (isem.irk.ru/conferences/mopt2017/Abstracts/BAIKAL_2017_paper_138.pdf): the smallest cubic graphs without 4-, 8- and 16-cycles have 78 vertices, found with canonical augmentation and 'probabilistic checking of every node'; no certificate, no full paper found; covers every cubic graph on at most 76 vertices. (b) Ducoffe-Dumitru, arXiv 2609.28594 v1: bipartite graphs of minimum degree 3 and order at most 66 by SAT modulo symmetries, forbidding 4, 8, 16, 32 (and 64 at orders 64-66), no proof log. (c) Garcia, arXiv 2609.04686: cites 'Exoo gave 54 <= f(4) <= 78'. None of (Tranquilli, Ducoffe-Dumitru, Garcia) cites Ripatti.

Coverage lemma (Tranquilli Prop. 10 for both root modes): with root {0,1,2} (arbitrary-root mode) or the triangle roots plus orbit 1 or 2, every connected linear v_3-configuration with v <= cap and no Berge 4- or 8-cycle appears as a completion of the growth tree, because the schedule is the lexicographic least-unfinished-point schedule with first-occurrence labels and the structural, C8 and C16 tests are monotone under sub-configurations. Re-derived independently by the producer and by the auditor (AUDIT.md section 1); NOT formalised. Empirical validation with both filters off: canonical class counts 1, 1, 3, 10, 31, 229, 2036 for v = 7..13 in both modes equal the nauty genbg -c sets exactly (set equality), and the auditor extended the check to v = 13 arbitrary root and v = 14 triangle roots (21,398 classes, set equal to genbg -c).

Positive controls, run before any headline number: P1 cap 29 reproduces Tranquilli Table 2 exactly in both orbits (1,405 / 106,964 / 7,184 / 63,526 / 34,850 / 0 and 20,088 / 1,655,404 / 113,012 / 1,208,473 / 313,832 / 0), the auditor's independent search reproduces them and the producer's transcript hash; 19-block states 46 + 291 = 337; P2c genbg -d3:3 -D3:3 -Z1 with an independent DFS cycle filter finds no C4/C8/C16-free cubic bipartite graph for v = 7..16 (producer) and v = 7..15 (auditor: 1, 1, 3, 10, 31, 229, 2036, 21,399, 245,342 C4-free graphs, every one with a C8); P3 C16 filter off, cap 19: completions exist, one isomorphism class, C4/C8-free with a C16 (16 labelled leaves with triangle roots, 128 with the arbitrary root; the class is self-dual with a colour-preserving automorphism group of order 57, 114 as an uncoloured Levi graph, so 128 labelled copies of one configuration are consistent with the paper's '128 symmetric 19_3-configurations').

Negative controls: N1 C8 filter off (C16 on), cap 13: completions appear, the Fano plane (v = 7) is the only class; N2 C8 filter on, cap 8: 0 completions in all three modes, with it off Fano (v = 7) and 8_3 (v = 8) appear and the checker accepts when completions are allowed; the Heawood graph (girth 6, 21 eight-cycles) is rejected by the C8 test on its last block; N3 tamper tests: truncated stream, flipped counter, corrupted C8 witness, wrong-length C16 witness, C16 relabelled as structural, deleted record, trailing data, inserted fake completion are all rejected by cb_check.py and cb_check_fast; the auditor's own tamper.py (11 further kinds: witness ending at an unintroduced point, non-simple walk, C16 witness cut to length 12, G re-tagged 8, deleted S, duplicated S, swapped records, false S, subtree replaced by S, header cap changed, header orbit changed) is rejected by all three checkers (cb_check.py, cb_check_fast, aud_check); verdicts as reported in AUDIT.md section 3 (the tampered streams are not shipped, 3.4 MB each; tamper.py regenerates them).

Route 1 (triangle-rooted, Tranquilli's mode), caps 30..34 (orders 60..68) and also cap 35 (order 70, girth-6 part only): both orbits close with 0 completions; oracle A (DFS endpoint sets, cached) and oracle B (join of complete half-path lists, uncached) give identical counters and identical FNV-1a decision-transcript hashes at every cap and orbit; the 12 certificate streams (134,625,781 bytes gzip in all, kept outside the bundle, names/sizes/sha256 in table_certs.tex and data/certs_inventory.json) are accepted by the producer's Python and C checkers and by the auditor's independent C checker aud_check (expected cap and orbit hard-coded, flags empty, c6 = 0); the auditor's own search and the producer's rebuilt binary reproduce all counters and hashes.

Route 2 (arbitrary root {0,1,2}, no triangle assumed, no Moore or cage premise), caps 29..34 (orders 58..68): 0 completions at every cap, oracles A and B give identical counters and transcript hashes, and the auditor's independent search reproduces every counter and hash. Cap 34: 13,798,102 states, 1,899,509,410 proposals, hash 76e8805d44433718. The cap-34 certificate stream (tens of GB, never stored) was regenerated by the producer's binary and streamed through a FIFO into cb_check_fast (accepted, data/main/R_cap34_checkfast.json), and regenerated again by the AUDITOR from a rebuilt binary and streamed into aud_check: ACCEPT, all counters equal, same stream sha256 0112b8085b969bcfa75335fdb2aedc5d4b5b0e80c6dddf2d5d9ead8f5a18fad5. The Python check of this stream was stopped unfinished and is not used.

Independent re-computation by the auditor (separate AI agent instance, 2026-10-31; own code, independent code but the same Prop. 10 schedule and the same kind of endpoint-set path test, so not an independent method): own search aud_search.c, own checker aud_check.c, own cycle filter aud_g6cyc.c; full enumeration with nauty-genbg -d3:3 -D3:3 -Z1 (disconnected graphs included) for v = 7..15 finds no graph without a 4-, 8- or 16-cycle (orders up to 30; every one has a C8); filter sanity checks (Heawood, Tutte-Coxeter, Petersen give C8; the cube gives C4; C10 gives none; C16 gives C16); the producer's cb_search.c and cb_check_fast.c rebuild to the frozen sha256 values. NOT done: genbg at v = 16 (stopped for cost).

HEADLINE (route 2, no premise). Every simple cubic bipartite graph on at most 68 vertices has a cycle of length 4, 8 or 16 (equivalently: no connected linear v_3-configuration with v <= 34 avoids Berge 4- and 8-cycles). Argument: a cubic bipartite graph has equal sides, so order <= 68 means v <= 34; a C4-free one is the Levi graph of a linear v_3-configuration, and a disconnected counterexample would contain a connected one of smaller order; the arbitrary-root search at cap 34 has no completion (EGC-C-0005); the coverage lemma (EGC-C-0001) is prose. This is a RE-CHECK, not a new bound: Ripatti 2017 (uncertified abstract) and Ducoffe-Dumitru 2026 (SAT, no proof log) cover these orders; we know of no earlier witness-checked computation. Filed C: exhaustive search plus witness checkers, no kernel check.

Route-1 reading of the graph statement: for order <= 60 the triangle-rooted search (EGC-C-0004) plus Tranquilli's Moore lemma suffices; for orders 62-68 it additionally needs n(3,10) = 70 (Tier L, read through a survey only), so the 62-68 part of route 1 is conditional; route 2 (EGC-C-0007) does not need it. The three (3,10)-cages (order 70) lie outside the triangle-rooted search; the route-1 cap-35 run is not a statement about order 70.

Absence claim, not a licence: we know of no earlier witness-checked (certificate-producing) computation for cubic bipartite orders 60-68. Basis: alphaXiv and web searches on 2026-10-28 (before the first run) and 2026-10-31 (which found Ripatti 2017, missed on 10-28), plus the auditor's search of OEIS/House of Graphs (one query each, not browsed). Residual risk: a certified computation exists in a source we did not find (Ripatti's full method, unpublished code). Not a priority claim.

NOT run or not complete: Lean/kernel formalisation (none, Tier C is the ceiling); pytest tests/ (not run); the repository guards antigravity_guard.py and test_rigor_guard.py exit 1 on pre-existing files elsewhere in the repository and flag no EG-CB68 file (logs/guard_*.txt); the Python check of the route-2 cap-34 stream (started 2026-10-31 14:41 UTC, stopped 17:34 UTC after at least 17.5 GB without rejection, partial hash deleted); the exploratory extension to caps >= 35 in arbitrary-root mode (cap 35 started 17:06 UTC, stopped 17:34 UTC, no result used); the auditor's genbg run at v = 16; any reading of O'Keefe-Wong 1980 or the full text of Ripatti 2017; a human audit. Recorded so the absences are explicit.
